questions.q: Match each step of the book's 'Chronology of reading ECG' to its correct position — 1) QRS complex 2) P wave 3) Rate 4) Axis 5) QT interval … A) Sixth B) First C) Fourth D) Fifth E) Second
questions.exp: The fixed chronology is: 1. QRS complex, 2. P wave, 3. Regularity of QRS (start from lead II / rhythm strip), 4. Rate, 5. Axis, 6. QT interval. (Book p377)

questions.q: Calibration note beside the 12-lead tracing: 1 small box = ____.
questions.exp: The book marks '1 small box = 40 ms' beside the tracing — i.e. 0.04 s, so 2.5 small boxes = 100 ms. (Book p377)

questions.q: The QRS complex produces the MAXIMUM deflection in the ECG because it represents:
questions.exp: Features of the QRS: maximum deflection in ECG, due to synchronous ventricular depolarisation. (Book p377)

questions.q: Normal / narrow QRS occupies 2–2.5 small boxes on the book's paper. In milliseconds and seconds that equals:
questions.exp: Normal/narrow QRS = 2–2.5 small boxes = 100 ms / 0.1 s (1 small box = 40 ms). (Book p377)

questions.q: Pick the ODD ONE OUT — the pairing that contradicts the book's QRS duration definitions:
questions.exp: Normal/narrow QRS is 2–2.5 small boxes (100 ms); wide QRS is > 0.12 s and very wide QRS is > 0.16 s. Calling a narrow QRS '> 0.12 s' is the odd one. (Book p377)

questions.q: Match each station of the route of depolarisation to the station it hands the impulse to NEXT — 1) Sinus node 2) AV node 3) Bundle of His 4) Left anterior fascicle … A) Bundle of His B) Purkinje fibres C) Atria D) Right & left bundle branches
questions.exp: Route: Sinus node → Atria → AV node → Bundle of His → Right BB / Left BB → (Left anterior & posterior fascicles) → Purkinje fibres → ventricles. (Book p378)

questions.q: TRUE or FALSE — per the book's note, ventricular depolarisation spreads from the epicardium towards the endocardium.
opts: True — the epicardium is reached first by Purkinje fibres
False — the note runs endocardium → epicardium
False — depolarisation has no transmural direction, only base-to-apex
True — the note actually describes repolarisation
questions.exp: The book's note is explicit: Depolarisation: Endocardium → Epicardium. (Book p378)

questions.q: Match each ventricular depolarisation event to its vector — 1) Septal depolarisation 2) Free wall depolarisation 3) Posterobasal LV depolarisation … A) Vector 3 B) Vector 1 C) Vector 2
questions.exp: Ventricular depolarisation: 1. Septal = Vector 1; 2. Free wall = Vector 2; 3. Posterobasal LV = Vector 3. (Book p378)

questions.q: The book's margin equation: QRS complex = Vector (____).
questions.exp: QRS complex = Vector (1 + 2 + 3) — septal, free-wall and posterobasal vectors summed. (Book p378)

questions.q: TRUE or FALSE — a DOWNWARD deflection is recorded when the flow of current is TOWARDS the positive electrode.
opts: True — the +ve electrode always draws the trace down
True — but only in the chest leads
False — downward deflection occurs when current flows AWAY from the +ve electrode; towards it the deflection is upward
False — deflection direction depends only on the −ve electrode
questions.exp: Flow of current: downward deflection if flow is away from the +ve electrode; upward deflection if flow is towards the +ve electrode. (Book p378)

questions.q: You wire a lead exactly like the book's diagram: right arm = −ve electrode (R), left arm = +ve electrode (L), galvanometer in between. A depolarisation wavefront now sweeps from the right arm towards the left arm. The galvanometer records:
opts: No deflection — the current is perpendicular to the lead
questions.exp: Current flowing towards the +ve electrode (left arm) records an upward deflection — case A in the book's flow-of-current figure. (Book p378)

questions.q: Vector 1 activates the LEFT side of the interventricular septum first because:
opts: The LBB is shorter than the RBB
The left septum has a lower stimulation threshold
The right septum is supplied by the left posterior fascicle
questions.exp: Vector 1 = IV septum; LBB shorter than RBB, hence the left side of the IV septum is activated first. (Book p379)

questions.q: Match each vector to its direction of spread — 1) Vector 1 2) Vector 2 3) Vector 3 … A) Superiorly & posteriorly B) Right side, anteriorly & inferiorly C) Rt → Lt, endocardium → epicardium (leftward, posteriorly & superiorly)
questions.exp: Vector 1: right side, anteriorly & inferiorly. Vector 2: Rt → Lt + endocardium → epicardium (left posteriorly & superiorly). Vector 3: superiorly & posteriorly. (Book p379)

questions.q: TRUE or FALSE — Vector 1 gives a positive deflection in right-sided leads, a negative deflection on the left side, and is the most predominant vector in the right lead.
opts: True — towards the right side it is positive, on the left negative, most predominant right lead
False — Vector 1 is positive on the left and negative on the right
False — Vector 1 is negative in all leads
True — but it is most predominant in the left lead
questions.exp: Vector 1: right-sided leads positive deflection, left-sided negative, and it is the most predominant, right lead. (Book p379)

questions.q: Vector 2 writes a ____ in V1 and a ____ in V5–V6.
opts: small q wave; tall T wave
questions.exp: Vector 2: right side −ve deflection in V1 → deep S wave; left side +ve in V5, V6 → big R. (Book p379)

questions.q: Three of these belong to Vector 3 as written in the book. Pick the ODD ONE OUT:
opts: Last part (posterobasal portion) to be depolarised
Most predominant vector, best seen in the right lead
questions.exp: Vector 3 = last (posterobasal) part, direction superiorly & posteriorly, no deflection. 'Most predominant, right lead' describes Vector 1. (Book p379)

questions.q: Match each chest lead to its surface position in the book's lead-position diagram — 1) V4 2) V5 3) V6 … A) Anterior axillary line B) Mid axillary line C) 5th ICS, midclavicular line
questions.exp: Position of leads: V4 at the 5th ICS on the midclavicular line, V5 on the anterior axillary line, V6 on the mid axillary line. (Book p379)

questions.q: Ventricular activation via an ALTERNATE pathway (myocardial cell-to-cell conduction) produces a wide QRS measuring:
questions.exp: Wide QRS cause 1: ventricular activation via alternate pathway — > 0.16 s, myocardial cell-to-cell conduction. (Book p379)

questions.q: Match each ventricular-generated rhythm to its rate — 1) Idioventricular 2) Accelerated idioventricular 3) Ventricular tachycardia … A) 40–100 bpm B) >100 bpm C) 15–40 bpm
questions.exp: Ventricular generated rhythm: idioventricular 15–40 bpm; accelerated idioventricular 40–100 bpm; ventricular tachycardia >100 bpm. (Book p379)

questions.q: Wide QRS via the NORMAL pathway with block measures ____ and corresponds to ____.
questions.exp: Cause 2: normal pathway with block — 0.12–0.16 s — Right Bundle Branch Block (RBBB) / Left BBB (LBBB). (Book p380)

questions.q: On the lead II rhythm strip you count 20 small boxes between two consecutive QRS complexes. Applying the book's formula (1500 / no. of small boxes b/w 2 QRS), the rate is:
questions.exp: Rate = 1500 / 20 = 75 bpm — inside the sinus range of 60–100 bpm. (Book p380)

questions.q: Match the pacemaker site to its rate range — 1) Sinus 2) Atrial / junctional 3) Ventricular … A) 15–40 bpm B) 60–100 bpm C) 40–60 bpm
questions.exp: Sinus rate 60–100 bpm; atrial/junctional rate 40–60 bpm; ventricular rate 15–40 bpm. (Book p380)

questions.q: TRUE or FALSE — 'Regularity of QRS' means the QRS complexes occur at regular, FIXED intervals.
opts: False — regularity permits gradually shortening intervals
False — regularity is judged on V1 only
True — but only when the rate exceeds 100 bpm
questions.exp: Regularity of QRS: QRS complexes occur at regular, fixed intervals. (Book p380)

questions.q: The P wave is the 1st wave of the ECG. It is produced by:
opts: Atrial depolarisation by the SA node
Atrial repolarisation by the AV node
questions.exp: P wave: 1st wave of ECG, due to atrial depolarisation by the SA node. (Book p380)

questions.q: Match each P-wave component to its meaning — 1) Ascending limb 2) Descending limb 3) Tall P >2.5 mm in leads II, III, aVF … A) Lt atrial depolarisation B) Rt atrial depolarisation C) P-pulmonale
questions.exp: Rt atrial depolarisation = ascending limb; Lt atrial depolarisation = descending limb; a P wave taller than 2.5 mm in II, III or aVF is labelled P-pulmonale. (Book p380)

questions.q: The 2.5/2.5 rule: normal height & width of the P wave = ____ mm.
questions.exp: 2.5/2.5 rule — height & width of P wave = 2.5 mm. (Book p380)

questions.q: TRUE or FALSE — the P wave is normal ONLY when the SA node depolarises the atria, and in normal sequence every QRS is preceded by a P wave.
opts: True — SA-nodal atrial activation plus a P before every QRS
False — a junctional P wave counts as normal too
False — only every second QRS needs a preceding P wave
True — but the AV node may replace the SA node without changing P morphology
questions.exp: Morphology: smooth, rounded; normal only when SA node depolarises atria; normal = every QRS is preceded by P wave. (Book p380)

questions.q: Pick the ODD ONE OUT — the descriptor that does NOT belong to the normal P wave in lead II per the book:
questions.exp: Normal P is smooth, rounded and upright in lead II; biphasic / inverted morphology belongs to lead V1, not lead II. (Book p380)

questions.q: The PR segment shows NO deflection on the tracing because the last leg of its journey (AV node → upper part of Bundle of His) is:
opts: Too fast for the galvanometer to record
questions.exp: PR segment parts: Atria → AV node; intra AV nodal (normal AV nodal delay); AV node → upper part of Bundle of His — electrically inert: no deflection. (Book p380)

questions.q: Match each stage of the PR segment journey to what happens there — 1) Atria 2) Intra AV nodal 3) AV node → … A) Normal AV nodal delay B) Upper part of Bundle of His C) AV node
questions.exp: Parts of the PR segment: Atria → AV node; intra AV nodal = normal AV nodal delay; AV node → upper part of Bundle of His. (Book p380)

questions.q: PR interval = P wave + PR segment = 0.12–0.2 s. On the book's paper that width equals how many small boxes?
questions.exp: PR interval 0.12–0.2 sec = 3–5 small boxes; > 0.2 s = prolonged PR interval. (Book p380)

questions.q: Match the abnormal PR interval to its mechanism — 1) Prolonged PR 2) Shortened PR … A) Aberrant pathway b/w atria & ventricle (Bundle of Kent) B) Defect / block on the regular pathway
questions.exp: Abnormal PR: prolonged = defect/block on regular pathway; shortened = aberrant pathway b/w atria & ventricle (Bundle of Kent). (Book p380)

questions.q: Narrow / normal QRS arm of the book's approach flowchart: match the PR / P-wave finding to the rhythm — 1) Normal PR & P wave 2) Short PR 3) Prolonged PR 4) Abnormal P wave 5) Absent P wave … A) 1° AV block B) Junctional rhythm C) SAN D) WPW E) Atrial rhythm
questions.exp: Look into PR interval: normal PR & P wave → SAN; short PR → WPW; prolonged PR → 1° AV block; abnormal P wave → atrial rhythm; absent P wave → junctional rhythm. (Book p381)

questions.q: Wide QRS arm of the flowchart: match the finding to its branch — 1) Wide QRS ≥ 0.16 s 2) Wide QRS 0.12–0.16 s 3) VT, idioventricular & accelerated idioventricular rhythms … A) Bundle Branch Block branch (RBBB / LBBB) B) Ventricular arrhythmia branch C) A rhythm sitting under the ≥ 0.16 s branch
questions.exp: Wide ≥ 0.16 s → ventricular arrhythmia (idioventricular rhythm, accelerated idioventricular rhythm, VT); wide 0.12–0.16 s → Bundle Branch Block (RBBB/LBBB). (Book p381)

questions.q: Match each bipolar lead to the two limbs it spans — 1) Lead I 2) Lead II 3) Lead III … A) Lt arm & Lt leg B) Rt arm & Lt arm C) Rt arm & Lt leg
questions.exp: Bipolar leads: Lead I b/w Rt arm & Lt arm; Lead II b/w Rt arm & Lt leg; Lead III b/w Lt arm & Lt leg. (Book p381)

questions.q: Match each augmented unipolar lead to the bipolar lead it is PERPENDICULAR to — 1) aVR 2) aVL 3) aVF … A) ⊥ to lead II B) ⊥ to lead I C) ⊥ to lead III
questions.exp: Augmented unipolar leads: aVR perpendicular to lead III; aVL ⊥ to lead II; aVF ⊥ to lead I. (Book p381)

questions.q: Match each lead to its angle on the book's hexaxial diagrams — 1) aVF 2) aVL 3) aVR 4) Lead III … A) −30° B) +90° C) −150° D) +120°
questions.exp: Hexaxial angles in the diagrams: I = 0°, II = +60°, III = +120°, aVF = +90°, aVL = −30°, aVR = −150°. (Book p381)

questions.q: Pick the ODD ONE OUT — the axis-zone pairing that CONTRADICTS the book's axis wheel:
opts: Northwest axis — a fixed, determinable value at +60°
questions.exp: On the wheel: normal axis ~0 to +90°, leftward/LAD −30 to −90°, RAD +90 to ±180°, and the northwest axis (aVR zone) CANNOT be determined — it is not a fixed +60°. (Book p382)

questions.q: Counting QRS heights in I, II, III, aVL & aVF, you find the two TALLEST complexes in lead II (+60°) and aVF (+90°). Per the book's rule, the axis lies:
questions.exp: Determining the axis: count QRS height in I, II, III, aVL & aVF; the axis lies b/w the 2 leads with max height — here between +60° and +90°. (Book p382)

questions.q: Axis shortcut: if a lead is EQUIPHASIC (R wave = S wave), the axis lies ____ to that lead.
questions.exp: Identify the equiphasic lead (R wave = S wave) → the axis lies ⊥ to it. (Book p382)

questions.q: The QT interval (ventricular repolarisation) is measured from:
opts: Beginning of the QRS complex to the end of the T wave
End of the QRS complex to the end of the T wave
Beginning of the P wave to the end of the T wave
Beginning of the QRS complex to the peak of the T wave
questions.exp: QT interval = beginning of QRS complex to end of T wave; equivalently QRS complex + ST segment + T wave. (Book p382)

questions.q: Pick the ODD ONE OUT — the QT value that does NOT match the book:
questions.exp: Book values: females 0.44 s, males 0.42 s, prolonged > 0.48 s. 'Males — 0.44 s' repeats the female value and is the odd one. (Book p382)

questions.q: TRUE or FALSE — the QT interval equals QRS complex + ST segment + T wave.
opts: True — QRS + ST segment + T wave
False — it excludes the ST segment
False — it equals QRS + T wave only
True — but only when the PR interval is normal
questions.exp: Features of QT: beginning of QRS to end of T; QRS complex + ST segment + T wave. (Book p382)

questions.q: Per the book, the upper normal QT duration quoted for FEMALES is:
questions.exp: QT: females 0.44 s; males 0.42 s; prolonged > 0.48 s. (Book p382)

units.title: ECG Interpretation & the QRS Complex
units.guide: Read the ECG in the book's fixed chronology: QRS → P wave → regularity (start on lead II / rhythm strip) → rate → axis → QT. Calibrate first: 1 small box = 40 ms. The QRS is the maximum deflection because ventricular depolarisation is synchronous; narrow = 2–2.5 small boxes (100 ms / 0.1 s), wide > 0.12 s, very wide > 0.16 s.

units.title: Route of Depolarisation & Current Flow
units.guide: Sinus node → atria → AV node → Bundle of His → bundle branches → fascicles → Purkinje fibres → ventricles; depolarisation runs endocardium → epicardium. Septal, free-wall and posterobasal events sum as QRS = Vector (1+2+3). Current TOWARDS the +ve electrode = upward deflection; AWAY = downward.

units.title: Ventricular Vectors & Chest Lead Positions
units.guide: Vector 1 (IV septum; LBB shorter than RBB) heads right-anterior-inferior — positive right, negative left, most predominant right lead. Vector 2 (free wall) runs Rt→Lt, endo→epi: deep S in V1, big R in V5–V6. Vector 3 (posterobasal, last) is superior-posterior with no deflection. V4 = 5th ICS midclavicular, V5 = anterior axillary, V6 = mid axillary line. Alternate-pathway wide QRS > 0.16 s: idioventricular 15–40, accelerated 40–100, VT >100 bpm.

units.title: Wide QRS Pathways, Rate & Regularity
units.guide: Wide QRS on a normal-but-blocked pathway = 0.12–0.16 s (RBBB / LBBB). Rate = 1500 ÷ small boxes between two QRS complexes; sinus 60–100, atrial/junctional 40–60, ventricular 15–40 bpm. Regularity = QRS complexes at regular, fixed intervals.

units.title: P Wave, PR Segment & PR Interval
units.guide: P wave = 1st wave, atrial depolarisation by the SA node; ascending limb = RA, descending limb = LA; 2.5/2.5 rule; smooth, rounded, upright in II (biphasic/inverted in V1); normal only with SA-nodal activation and a P before every QRS. PR segment (atria → His) ends electrically inert, hence flat. PR interval = P + PR segment = 0.12–0.2 s (3–5 boxes); prolonged = block on the regular pathway; shortened = Bundle of Kent.

units.title: Approach to the QRS & the Limb Leads
units.guide: Narrow QRS: normal PR & P → SAN; short PR → WPW; prolonged PR → 1° AV block; abnormal P → atrial rhythm; absent P → junctional rhythm. Wide ≥ 0.16 s → ventricular arrhythmia; 0.12–0.16 s → BBB. Bipolar: I = RA–LA, II = RA–LL, III = LA–LL. Augmented: aVR ⊥ III, aVL ⊥ II, aVF ⊥ I. Angles: I 0°, II +60°, III +120°, aVF +90°, aVL −30°, aVR −150°.

units.title: Axis Determination & the QT Interval
units.guide: Axis: count QRS heights in I, II, III, aVL, aVF — it lies between the two tallest; an equiphasic lead (R = S) puts the axis ⊥ to it. Zones: normal ~0 to +90°, LAD −30 to −90°, RAD +90 to ±180°, northwest (aVR zone) cannot be determined. QT = ventricular repolarisation = QRS + ST + T, from QRS start to T end; females 0.44 s, males 0.42 s, prolonged > 0.48 s.
